newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME metals little moved in Asia, Deng not a factor.
newsitem.headline: LME metals little moved in Asia, Deng not a factor.

text.p: London Metal Exchange prices barely moved during Asian trading hours on Thursday from Wednesday's after-hours levels, showing little reaction to Deng Xiaoping's death on Wednesday night, traders said.
Traders said Deng's passing had been expected for some time, while few expected any dramatic changes in Chinese economic policy in the near term.

One trader noted that the copper market appeared to be bumping up against downtrend resistance after a rally to eight-month highs on Wednesday, although he was expecting a near-term retest of resistance above $2,350 a tonne and perhaps a rise to $2,400.
At 0730 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper stood at $2,334/39 a tonne versus $2,333/35 at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and $2,340 at the afternoon kerb close.
LME three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,607/10 a tonne, up marginally from $1,605/09 at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and $1,604 at the afternoon kerb close.
Zinc was quoted at $1,229/33, little changed from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close of $1,230.
